debate-on-annual-budget-statement.title: Parliament debates Budget 2026
debate-on-annual-budget-statement.what_it_is: A parliamentary debate on Budget 2026, with MPs speaking and the Prime Minister responding to clarifications.
debate-on-annual-budget-statement.why_it_matters: MPs said Budget 2026 continues one-off support such as CDC vouchers and utilities rebates, and strengthens CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates for seniors. They also said it raises the monthly household income threshold for student care fee assistance to $6,500 and lowers PARF rebates by 45% with a $30,000 cap. The transcript records many further proposals, but does not state that they have been adopted.

an-economy-of-the-future-that-works-for-.title: Motion on Singapore's economic future, amended and agreed to
an-economy-of-the-future-that-works-for-.what_it_is: A Motion moved by Mr Kenneth Tiong and seconded by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, proposing principles for a more equal and inclusive economy and an economic engine driven by local companies, domestic demand and Singaporeans venturing abroad, which was debated and amended.
an-economy-of-the-future-that-works-for-.why_it_matters: The amended Motion records the House's belief in a more equal and inclusive economy and an economy powered by dynamic local companies, global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad. The transcript does not state any direct change to law or schemes from the Motion itself. The record does not set out the practical impact.

land-transport-and-related-matters-bill.title: Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, Second Reading debate
land-transport-and-related-matters-bill.what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, an omnibus Bill by the Ministry of Transport and Ministry of Home Affairs that amends road traffic, active mobility, ERP 2.0, speed limiter and related laws.
land-transport-and-related-matters-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill decriminalises missed ERP charges and makes the On-Board Unit mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles from 1 January 2027. It lowers the speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths to six kilometres an hour from 1 June 2026, requires a Certificate of Medical Need for mobility scooter users on public paths, and introduces registration and penalties. It also raises penalties for illegal vehicle modifications and unregistered or deregistered vehicles, and updates speed limiter offences.

committee-of-supply-head-k-ministry-of-e.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Education budget
committee-of-supply-head-k-ministry-of-e.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head K, the Ministry of Education, with Members moving cuts and the Minister and Ministers of State responding.
committee-of-supply-head-k-ministry-of-e.why_it_matters: The debate records changes to primary and secondary education, including the GEP refresh, a single Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise from 2028, Higher Mother Tongue eligibility from Secondary 1, and more financial assistance for lower- to middle-income students from Academic Year 2026. It also records reviews of Primary 1 registration, class sizes, milestone exams and DSA, and a salary review for educators.

committee-of-supply-head-s-ministry-of-m.title: Committee of Supply debate on Manpower Ministry budget and labour policies
committee-of-supply-head-s-ministry-of-m.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head S (Manpower) of the Estimates, opened by Ms Yeo Wan Ling moving a $100 reduction amendment, with MPs raising labour policy proposals and ministers responding.
committee-of-supply-head-s-ministry-of-m.why_it_matters: The transcript records planned changes including adding eight occupations to the NTS-OL in 2026, raising EP and S Pass qualifying salaries and the Local Qualifying Salary, extending GRIT to the 2026 cohort, and expanding the Overseas Markets Immersion Programme. It also records proposals from MPs on retrenchment benefits, jobseeker support, caregiver leave, and wage thresholds, but does not state that these proposals will be adopted.

health-information-bill.title: Health Information Bill Second Reading debate
health-information-bill.what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Health Information Bill, which requires licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to the National Electronic Health Record and sets rules for access, sharing and safeguards.
health-information-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill requires all licensed healthcare providers and retail pharmacies to contribute key health information to NEHR, so a patient's records can follow them across providers. It allows patients to restrict access, while critical allergies and vaccination records remain visible, and prohibits access for employment or insurance purposes. The Minister says the Bill is intended to take effect from early 2027.

singapore-sports-council-amendment-bill.title: Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
singapore-sports-council-amendment-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to amend the Singapore Sports Council Act, expanding SportSG's functions to include physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports, and updating its powers over standards, institutions and athlete support.
singapore-sports-council-amendment-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill expands what is legally recognised as sport to include mind sports and e-sports and physical fitness activities, and gives SportSG powers to set standards and establish athlete-training institutions. It also recognises the Singapore National Paralympic Council as a key partner and increases the maximum SportSG Board size from 15 to 25. The Minister said the changes are to empower SportSG to more effectively administer its role in driving all Singaporeans to live better through sport.

committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Prime Minister's Office budget
committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head U (Prime Minister's Office) of the Estimates, with MPs moving cuts and ministers responding on public service, research and innovation, climate policy, population, cash and banking access, and insurance.
committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head U of the Estimates
committee-of-supply-head-u-prime-ministe.why_it_matters: The transcript states that the carbon tax has increased to $45 per tonne this year, that households will receive additional U-Save rebates to manage energy costs, and that HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores. It also records that MAS is monitoring cash acceptance and may consider making cash acceptance mandatory by law.

committee-of-supply-head-v-ministry-of-t.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Trade and Industry budget
committee-of-supply-head-v-ministry-of-t.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head V of the Ministry of Trade and Industry's budget, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' cuts and ministerial responses.
committee-of-supply-head-v-ministry-of-t.why_it_matters: The debate covers MTI's budget and policy directions, including support for SMEs, internationalisation, energy, and consumer protection. It records that public consultations on consumer protection will begin on 16 March 2026, and that the Government will reassess GDP and inflation forecasts if necessary. The record does not state that the specific proposals raised by Members were adopted.

expression-of-regret-at-the-conduct-of-m.title: Parliament debates and votes on motion on Pritam Singh's conduct and suitability as Leader of the Opposition
expression-of-regret-at-the-conduct-of-m.what_it_is: A motion moved by the Leader of the House asking Parliament to affirm honesty and integrity, note court and Committee of Privileges findings, express regret at Mr Pritam Singh's conduct, consider him unsuitable to continue as Leader of the Opposition, note implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, and call on MPs to uphold the law.
expression-of-regret-at-the-conduct-of-m.why_it_matters: The transcript states the Motion does not impose penalties or sanctions on Mr Pritam Singh under the PPIPA and does not itself remove the Leader of the Opposition; that designation is for the Prime Minister to decide. The House voted, the Ayes had it, and dissent was recorded for named Members. The Motion also asks the House to note that the High Court judgment and COP findings have implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, to be considered separately.

committee-of-supply-head-n-ministry-of-f.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs budget
committee-of-supply-head-n-ministry-of-f.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head N, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved to reduce the total sum by $100 and Members questioned ministers on foreign policy.
committee-of-supply-head-n-ministry-of-f.why_it_matters: The record says foreign policy shapes Singapore's food security, energy resilience, jobs and safety abroad, and that supply-chain disruption affects jobs, cost of living and business confidence. It also records MFA consular assistance for Singaporeans overseas, including during emergencies.

an-artificial-intelligence-ai-transition.title: Motion on AI-enabled growth and support for workers and enterprises
an-artificial-intelligence-ai-transition.what_it_is: A Motion moved by Mr Ng Chee Meng setting out four commitments on AI-enabled economic growth, fairness, worker and enterprise support, and inclusive progress, followed by debate and a ministerial response.
an-artificial-intelligence-ai-transition.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out measures that affect workers and businesses: from the second half of this year, Singaporeans enrolled in selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive six months of free access to premium AI tools; eligible businesses will receive $10,000 under the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit later this year; and all IHLs will offer selected AI-related courses for alumni at a significant discount for a year starting in the second half of this year. It also records that the Government will study improvements to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme and that tripartite partners are discussing shortening retrenchment notification under the Employment Act review.

reinforcing-singapore-s-position-as-a-gl.title: Motion on strengthening Singapore's economic competitiveness as a globally connected aviation, maritime and logistics hub
reinforcing-singapore-s-position-as-a-gl.what_it_is: A Motion moved by the Chairperson of the Government Parliamentary Committee for Transport, Ms Tin Pei Ling, affirming the importance of strengthening Singapore's long-term economic competitiveness through international cooperation, frontier technologies and world-class infrastructure, debated by Members and resolved by the House.
reinforcing-singapore-s-position-as-a-gl.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out concrete measures: MOT plans to invest $800 million over the next five years on transport research and innovation, and a manpower transition package for taxi and private-hire drivers includes place-and-train Career Conversion Programmes launching in the third quarter of this year, a $20-per-hour training incentive from January 2027, and a one-stop information webpage. Autonomous shuttles already run in Punggol and autonomous buses will be piloted on Service 400 in Marina Bay and Service 191 in One-North.

road-traffic-miscellaneous-amendments-bi.title: Second Reading of the Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill
road-traffic-miscellaneous-amendments-bi.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Second Minister for Home Affairs on behalf of the Senior Minister, amending the Road Traffic Act to strengthen penalties for dangerous driving, tighten alcohol limits, create a drug-driving offence, and enhance enforcement.
road-traffic-miscellaneous-amendments-bi.why_it_matters: The Bill creates a new offence of purposeful endangerment carrying up to 15 years' imprisonment and lifetime disqualification, lowers the prescribed alcohol limits, makes holding a mobile phone while a vehicle is in motion an offence, and introduces a presence-based drug-driving offence. It also allows automated notices for traffic offences and tightens the Driver Improvement Points System from January 2027.

skills-and-workforce-development-agency-.title: Bill to merge SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into a new Skills and Workforce Development Agency
skills-and-workforce-development-agency-.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to establish the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) by merging SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore and transferring their functions, employees and assets.
skills-and-workforce-development-agency-.why_it_matters: The Bill establishes SWDA as a statutory board whose functions cover the existing functions of SSG and WSG and extend to promoting career and employment services and training. If passed, SWDA will be established in the third quarter of 2026, and employees of WSG and SSG will transfer on terms no less favourable than their present ones. The Minister said SSG's and WSG's operations will be fully undertaken by SWDA from Day One, with existing grant and employment assistance commitments honoured.

committee-of-supply-head-x-ministry-of-c.title: Committee of Supply debate on MCCY and Muslim Affairs, ending with withdrawal of $100 reduction
committee-of-supply-head-x-ministry-of-c.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head X of the Estimates for the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, opened by Mr Alex Yam moving a $100 reduction and covering Muslim Affairs and MCCY clarifications.
committee-of-supply-head-x-ministry-of-c.why_it_matters: The transcript records planned changes to marriage and parenthood support, including expanding Bersamamu and making Project ARIF permanent from June 2026, and to education support through MENDAKI programmes and a Tampines after-school pilot. It also records mosque planning, the SCIS opening in 2028, WMS fundraising, and MCCY measures such as SpexSG taking effect from 1 April and SG Partnerships Fund co-funding. The record does not set out the full practical impact of every measure.

committee-of-supply-head-t-ministry-of-n.title: MND budget debate: housing, lift access, ageing estates and pest birds
committee-of-supply-head-t-ministry-of-n.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head T of the Estimates for the Ministry of National Development, opened by Mr Henry Kwek moving a $100 reduction and ending with him seeking leave to withdraw the amendment.
committee-of-supply-head-t-ministry-of-n.why_it_matters: The debate covers HDB affordability, public rental, lift access, ageing estates, executive condominiums and pest birds. The transcript records that public rental has had no income ceiling since 2023, that HDB will look to implement lift access for 40 identified blocks within the next three years, and that a pigeon netting trial for 35 units will run from March to next March. Other proposals remain under review or without stated timelines.

committee-of-supply-head-o-ministry-of-h.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Health budget
committee-of-supply-head-o-ministry-of-h.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head O, Ministry of Health, including an amendment to reduce the allocation by $100 and ministerial responses on healthcare financing, preventive care, workforce and mental health.
committee-of-supply-head-o-ministry-of-h.why_it_matters: The Ministry announced higher MediSave withdrawal limits for chronic and preventive care from January 2027, subsidised genetic testing for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer from December this year, and extension of MediShield Life and MediSave to cover preventive surgeries for HBOC later this year. It also set out community health posts and specialist-supported care in Woodlands, and an AI risk assessment tool for Healthier SG enrolees from early 2027.

impact-of-the-middle-east-situation-on-s.title: Ministerial statements on the Middle East conflict and support measures for Singapore
impact-of-the-middle-east-situation-on-s.what_it_is: A series of ministerial statements addressing parliamentary questions on the impact of the Middle East situation on Singapore, followed by grouped clarifications from ministers.
impact-of-the-middle-east-situation-on-s.why_it_matters: The statements set out support measures including $200 cash for active platform workers, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers from the end of the month; enhanced U-Save rebates; $500 CDC vouchers brought forward to June 2026; and a $200 increase to the Budget 2026 Cost-of-Living Special Payment, with about 2.4 million Singaporeans receiving cash in September. They also state that the regulated electricity tariff is expected to rise more sharply in the next adjustment and that overall inflation for 2026 is expected to be higher than earlier projected.

committee-of-supply-head-w-ministry-of-t.title: Committee of Supply debate on transport spending and policy
committee-of-supply-head-w-ministry-of-t.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head W of the Estimates, opened by Ms Tin Pei Ling moving a $100 reduction, followed by Member speeches and ministerial clarifications on transport policy.
committee-of-supply-head-w-ministry-of-t.why_it_matters: The transcript records a transport spending debate covering airport and port expansion, EV charging, autonomous vehicles, rail timelines, bus connectivity, road safety and COE reform. The only formal action is the withdrawal of the proposed $100 reduction in Head W, so the record does not show a spending change taking effect. The record does not set out the practical impact of the proposals beyond the stated questions and ministerial responses.

committee-of-supply-head-i-ministry-of-s.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Social and Family Development budget
committee-of-supply-head-i-ministry-of-s.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Social and Family Development budget, opened by Mr Xie Yao Quan moving a $100 reduction to Head I of the Estimates, with MPs raising policy asks and ministers setting out MSF plans.
committee-of-supply-head-i-ministry-of-s.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out changes including a new $500 quarterly Partnership Payout for all ComLink+ families, a rise in the Student Care Fee Assistance income threshold from $4,500 to $6,500 benefiting around 13,000 students, and from January 2027 a higher gross monthly household income ceiling of $15,000 for childcare and Kindergarten Fee Assistance. It also states that from July 2026 subsidies for residential and community disability services will rise by up to 15 and 10 percentage points, and that filing Form 1 of an LPA will be free for citizens.

veterinary-practice-bill.title: Veterinary Practice Bill at Second Reading, creating a Veterinary Council to register and discipline vets
veterinary-practice-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Minister of State for National Development on behalf of the Minister for National Development, that establishes a Veterinary Council to register veterinarians and regulate the practice of veterinary medicine in Singapore.
veterinary-practice-bill.why_it_matters: The Minister said vets will have to be registered with the new Council and hold a valid practising certificate to practise, and that the Registrar must publish registered vets' particulars so the public can search for and verify a vet's registration status and place of practice. The maximum financial penalty for unlawful practice or misrepresentation as a vet rises from $10,000 to $50,000. Existing AVS-licensed vets will be temporarily deemed duly qualified and must obtain registration and a practising certificate within a stipulated grace period to continue practising.

committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.title: MINDEF budget debate and withdrawn $100 amendment
committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head J (Ministry of Defence) of the Estimates, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved and later withdrew an amendment to reduce the allocation by $100.
committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head J of the Estimates
committee-of-supply-head-j-ministry-of-d.why_it_matters: The Minister said MINDEF/SAF will build a suite of conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities, acquire three Gulfstream G550 maritime surveillance aircraft, and scale unmanned platforms paired with manned platforms. He also said MINDEF will take care of NSmen and NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance where budget space allows, regularly review NSF allowances, and do more for HOME awards, NS credits and tax incentives where possible. The debate also covered cross-domain cooperation with other agencies and new international partnerships on cyber, information warfare and critical underwater infrastructure.

committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment budget
committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head L of the Estimates for the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, covering climate adaptation, water, food, heat, waste and related policies.
committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head L of the Estimates
committee-of-supply-head-l-ministry-of-s.why_it_matters: The transcript states that from April the Beverage Container Return Scheme will add a 10-cent deposit on marked beverage containers, refundable at reverse vending machines, and that climate vouchers will be expanded next month to include five-tick clothes dryers and induction stoves. It also states that 2026 is designated the Year of Climate Adaptation, that a National Adaptation Plan will be published in 2027, and that portable flood barriers and flood alerts are being made available to residents.

committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.title: Committee of Supply debate on Ministry of Home Affairs Head P
committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head P of the Estimates for the Ministry of Home Affairs, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' speeches and ministerial responses.
committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.stage: Committee of Supply (Head P of the Estimates)
committee-of-supply-head-p-ministry-of-h.why_it_matters: The debate covers Home Team policies on terrorism, cyberattacks, drugs, scams, rehabilitation, fire safety and road safety. The transcript states specific changes including extending Fire Certificate validity from one year to three years from 1 April 2026, planning to bring RHA measures into force by end-2026, and amending FICA to allow anticipatory directions against online communications.

committee-of-supply-head-q-ministry-of-d.title: Committee of Supply debate on MDDI Head Q: AI adoption, online safety and cybersecurity
committee-of-supply-head-q-ministry-of-d.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Digital Development and Information's Head Q budget, opened by Mr Sharael Taha moving a $100 reduction and followed by ministerial responses.
committee-of-supply-head-q-ministry-of-d.why_it_matters: The debate covers measures intended to help more local enterprises adopt AI, with the National AI Impact Programme aiming to support 10,000 local enterprises over three years. It also covers online safety, scam and misinformation risks, and a planned AI translation tool to make public-facing materials more accessible to non-English speakers. The record does not quantify the effect on households or individual workers beyond these stated aims.

national-council-of-social-service-amend.title: Second Reading of the National Council of Social Service (Amendment) Bill
national-council-of-social-service-amend.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to amend the National Council of Social Service Act, moved by the Minister for Social and Family Development, updating NCSS's objectives, membership, Council governance and related statutory provisions.
national-council-of-social-service-amend.why_it_matters: The Bill updates NCSS's statutory objectives and functions to strengthen social service delivery, build sector capabilities and develop the broader social service ecosystem. It introduces a single-tier sector membership and a fully appointed Council, and extends ComChest's role beyond fundraising. The record says these changes are intended to improve outcomes for service users and support those in need.

energy-conservation-amendment-bill.title: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
energy-conservation-amendment-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading that extends Minimum Energy Performance Standards and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use, and empowers the Minister to make regulations for online platforms to remove non-compliant listings.
energy-conservation-amendment-bill.why_it_matters: From 1 July 2026, end users importing regulated goods for their own use are to register with NEA, meet MEPS and carry MELS labels, with fines up to $10,000 per import for non-compliance. Registration and renewal fees for end users are to be waived, and existing schemes such as the Energy Efficiency Grant and Climate Vouchers are cited as support. The Bill excludes second-hand or used regulated goods and regulated lamps.

committee-of-supply-head-r-ministry-of-l.title: Ministry of Law Committee of Supply debate and vote on a $100 budget cut
committee-of-supply-head-r-ministry-of-l.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Law's budget, including a proposed $100 reduction moved by Mr Vikram Nair, which was put to a vote.
committee-of-supply-head-r-ministry-of-l.why_it_matters: The debate sets out plans to expand civil legal aid to more households, with the per capita household income threshold rising from $1,050 to $1,650 and the savings threshold from $10,000 to $12,000, targeted for later this year. It also covers reforms to civil judgment enforcement, including new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers, with a Bill planned later this year. The proposed $100 reduction to the Ministry of Law's budget was put to a vote and the 'Noes' had it.

securities-and-futures-amendment-bill.title: Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading: dual listings and the Global Listing Board
securities-and-futures-amendment-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by Mr Chee Hong Tat on behalf of the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, that introduces a framework for dual listings between SGX and eligible overseas exchanges and makes other amendments to the Securities and Futures Act.
securities-and-futures-amendment-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill is intended to let issuers use one prospectus and harmonised rules to list concurrently on SGX and an overseas exchange, starting with the Global Listing Board with Nasdaq, and to reduce compliance costs. It also allows issuers to engage retail investors using preliminary prospectuses, subject to safeguards, and clarifies that the company issuing underlying shares, not the depositary, lodges the prospectus for depositary receipt offerings. The record says investors will also gain access to a broader range of high-quality investment opportunities and that Singapore investors will continue to be able to seek recourse for losses arising from such breaches under the investor recourse provisions in the SFA.

statutes-miscellaneous-amendments-bill.title: Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill debated and read a Third time
statutes-miscellaneous-amendments-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, the Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill, making miscellaneous amendments to several Acts, including BCA, URA, COTMA, Architects Act, Professional Engineers Act, HDB Act, Wildlife Act and Endangered Species Act.
statutes-miscellaneous-amendments-bill.stage: Second Reading, Committee stage, and Third Reading
statutes-miscellaneous-amendments-bill.why_it_matters: The record says the Bill expands BCA's functions to manage programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme for private residential estates and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme, and expands URA's role to coordinate transport, utilities and other infrastructure planning. It also validates past fees and charges collected by BCA, HDB, NParks and URA, raises maximum penalties for wildlife feeding, and changes rules for professional registration and hybrid plants. The record does not set out the aggregate number of people affected or total sums involved in the validated fees.

coastal-protection-and-other-amendments-.title: Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill at Second Reading
coastal-protection-and-other-amendments-.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment, to amend the Sewerage and Drainage Act and related laws to create a coastal protection framework, including PUB powers, landowner obligations, grants and enforcement.
coastal-protection-and-other-amendments-.why_it_matters: The Minister said sea levels may rise up to 1.15 metres by the end of this century and up to five metres with storm surges and high tides, and that around 30% of Singapore could be flooded by seawater. The Bill creates obligations for owners of Prescribed Places to put coastal protection measures in place by a stipulated date, with PUB coordinating and enforcing a continuous line of defence. It also provides for a capital grant and technical advice to support landowners.

public-sector-governance-amendment-bill.title: Public Sector (Governance) (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
public-sector-governance-amendment-bill.what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Public Sector (Governance) (Amendment) Bill, which would allow public agencies to share data with trusted external partners under safeguards and create related offences for misuse.
public-sector-governance-amendment-bill.why_it_matters: The Minister said the amendments will enable vulnerable Singaporeans to receive faster, targeted and more coordinated support, when they need it most. She also said families in need currently repeat their stories and details to many parties, and the Bill introduces criminal offences for individuals in external organisations who misuse shared data. The record does not set out commencement dates or other practical impacts beyond these stated aims.

cross-border-railways-border-control-co-.title: Cross-Border Railways (Border Control Co-location) Bill at Second Reading
cross-border-railways-border-control-co-.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Second Minister for Home Affairs, to give effect to co-located customs, immigration and quarantine facilities and related cross-border railway arrangements for the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link.
cross-border-railways-border-control-co-.why_it_matters: The Minister said the RTS Link is targeted to commence service this December, with peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour per direction, and will help relieve congestion on the Causeway. Under the co-located model, passengers undergo both departure and arrival immigration clearance before boarding the train and no further immigration clearance is required upon disembarkation in the other country. The Bill also sets out arrangements for cross-border incident management and concurrent criminal jurisdiction on trains in transit.

tobacco-control-of-advertisements-and-sa.title: Bill to rename and broaden tobacco control law to cover vaporisers and psychoactive substances
tobacco-control-of-advertisements-and-sa.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by Senior Minister of State for Health Dr Koh Poh Koon, to amend the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act 1993, rename it the Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act, control vaporisers and specified psychoactive substances, and provide for rehabilitation and penalties.
tobacco-control-of-advertisements-and-sa.why_it_matters: The Bill increases the maximum fine for purchase, use and possession of vaporisers from $2,000 to $10,000, and introduces mandatory imprisonment and higher fines for import and supply. It creates rehabilitation orders for people who consume specified psychoactive substances and for repeat vaporiser users, and places duties on owners and occupiers of specified premises and storage spaces. The Senior Minister of State said the Government intends for the Bill to commence on 1 May.

central-provident-fund-amendment-bill.title: CPF (Amendment) Bill — transfer of Singtel Special Discounted Shares to CDP accounts
central-provident-fund-amendment-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading that amends the CPF Act to enable the transfer of Singtel Special Discounted Shares from the CPF Board to CDP accounts of SDS holders.
central-provident-fund-amendment-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill enables the transfer of Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to CDP accounts for around 615,000 SDS holders, planned for November 2026. Holders with individual CDP accounts will have their shares transferred there, while those without will have designated CDP accounts created under their names. Holders may sell and receive proceeds in their CPF Ordinary Account or in cash, with CPF withdrawal conditions waived from 8 April 2026.

annual-budget-statement.title: Singapore Budget 2026 statement and motion to approve FY2026/2027 financial policy
annual-budget-statement.what_it_is: A Budget statement by the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance moving a motion for Parliament to approve the Government's financial policy for FY2026/2027, followed by adjournment of the debate.
annual-budget-statement.why_it_matters: The Budget sets out changes including a 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate for companies, a higher Local Qualifying Salary from $1,600 to $1,800, CPF top-ups of up to $1,500 for Singaporeans aged 50 and above with lower retirement savings, $500 Child LifeSG Credits, and cost-of-living payments of $200 to $400. It also raises Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries from January 2027 and increases tobacco excise duty by 20% with effect from today.

info-communications-media-development-au.title: Second Reading of the IMDA (Amendment) Bill
info-communications-media-development-au.what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on a Bill to amend the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act and make related amendments to the Telecommunications Act, aligning media-sector regulation with telecommunications regulation.
info-communications-media-development-au.why_it_matters: The Bill would require IMDA approval for acquisitions of 30% or more of a regulated media entity and allow IMDA to issue directions on market conduct and consumer protection. It would also allow the Minister to order structural separation as a last resort. The record does not set out specific price, service or employment outcomes.

committee-of-supply-head-m-ministry-of-f.title: Ministry of Finance Committee of Supply debate on fiscal stewardship, tax thresholds and procurement
committee-of-supply-head-m-ministry-of-f.what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head M (Ministry of Finance), where MPs moved cuts to the allocation and ministers responded on fiscal policy, tax, procurement and business support.
committee-of-supply-head-m-ministry-of-f.why_it_matters: The record sets out changes for businesses: Tender Lite for ICT procurement will launch from April 2026, and all GST-registered businesses must submit digital invoices via InvoiceNow by April 2031. For individuals, the Minister said the $20,000 personal income tax exemption threshold will be regularly reviewed, and the GST display concession for F&B and hotels will be reviewed in future. The amendment to reduce Head M by $100 was withdrawn.

grant-to-imf-s-poverty-reduction-and-gro.title: Parliament approves grants to IMF trust funds for low-income countries and Sudan's debt relief
grant-to-imf-s-poverty-reduction-and-gro.what_it_is: Two Motions moved by Minister of State Alvin Tan under section 6A(2)(d) of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act 1966, asking Parliament to fix the maximum amount of grants the Monetary Authority of Singapore may give to the IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust and to the PRG-HIPC Trust for Sudan's debt relief, debated together and voted on separately.
grant-to-imf-s-poverty-reduction-and-gro.why_it_matters: The transcript states that the grant to the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust will draw from Singapore's 2021 SDR allocation and reduce MAS' official foreign reserves by 21 million SDR, about US$28.6 million, while the grant to the PRG-HIPC Trust will be funded from Singapore's share of the IMF's existing resources and will not affect the size of MAS' official foreign reserves. Minister of State Alvin Tan said the contributions do not draw on past reserves and will not affect or reduce domestic expenditure for Singaporeans. The money supports the IMF's concessional lending to low-income countries and Sudan's debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative.

info-communications-media-developmemnt-a.title: Bill to align competition rules for Singapore's media and telecom sectors
info-communications-media-developmemnt-a.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading that amends the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act to harmonise competition rules for the telecommunications and media sectors and strengthen IMDA's regulatory toolkit.
info-communications-media-developmemnt-a.why_it_matters: The Bill is intended to protect consumer interests by keeping the media market competitive and fair, with public confidence, good content, reasonable prices and a vibrant information environment. It also gives IMDA tools to act when fair market conduct is threatened and where service providers' actions may hurt consumer interests. The transcript also notes that workers may face disruption from mergers or restructurings, and that MOM frameworks and union engagement continue.

reaching-75-reforming-singapore-s-public.title: Adjournment speech on public transport: bus contracting, rail financing and autonomous vehicles
reaching-75-reforming-singapore-s-public.what_it_is: An adjournment motion moved by the Deputy Leader of the House, followed by an adjournment speech by Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis setting out proposals on buses, rail and autonomous vehicles, and a response from the Senior Minister of State for Transport, Ms Sun Xueling.
reaching-75-reforming-singapore-s-public.why_it_matters: The transcript sets out planned changes to public transport: the rail network is to grow from 275 kilometres today to about 360 kilometres by the early 2030s, and more than half of bus services now run at intervals of 10 minutes or less during peak. Six autonomous buses have been procured and are due to start operating on Bus Services 400 and 191 in the second half of 2026.

curiosity-credits-empowering-informed-po.title: Adjournment Motion on Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary school students
curiosity-credits-empowering-informed-po.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion speech by Mr David Hoe proposing Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary school students, followed by a response from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi, before Parliament adjourned.
curiosity-credits-empowering-informed-po.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

make-singapore-equities-great-again.title: Adjournment Motion on strengthening Singapore's equities market
make-singapore-equities-great-again.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion debate in which Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis and Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim set out proposals for Singapore's equities market and Minister Chee Hong Tat responds on the Government's review and measures.
make-singapore-equities-great-again.why_it_matters: The Minister says the measures aim to make the market more competitive and to increase investor participation, and that MAS will take steps to strengthen investor confidence and enhance investor protection mechanisms, especially for retail investors. He also reports that average daily traded value on SGX grew more than 20% year-on-year to almost $1.8 billion in November 2025, IPO activity raised more than $2.4 billion last year, and SGX total market value crossed $1 trillion.

rethinking-redevelopment-and-green-prese.title: Adjournment motion on land use, green spaces and the Serangoon River Forest bus depot
rethinking-redevelopment-and-green-prese.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion in which Dennis Tan called for a rethink of how development and green space trade-offs are assessed, and Minister of State Alvin Tan responded on land use planning and the Serangoon River Forest bus depot.
rethinking-redevelopment-and-green-prese.why_it_matters: The record states the planned bus depot at the southern part of the Serangoon area is intended to improve public transport services for residents and bring economic development and jobs closer to homes in Hougang, Sengkang, Defu and Paya Lebar Air Base. LTA has agreed to measures during construction, including hoarding the work site and conducting checks for birds' nests and other wildlife before site clearance. The Minister said the Government will not revisit the matter.

fire-safety-in-our-homes.title: Adjournment Motion on fire safety in homes
fire-safety-in-our-homes.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion where a Non-Constituency Member spoke on fire safety in homes and the Minister of State for Home Affairs responded.
fire-safety-in-our-homes.why_it_matters: The Minister said the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill was introduced for First Reading, which makes it an offence to keep unsafe devices such as non-UL2272 certified e-scooters. He also said MOT targets legislative amendments later this year to strengthen regulations on online sale of AMDs. The record does not set out other practical impacts of the proposals raised.

an-industrial-policy-in-finance.title: Gold as a reserve asset and Singapore's pitch to become a gold trading hub
an-industrial-policy-in-finance.what_it_is: An adjournment motion debate in which Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat set out a five-part proposal for Singapore to build a gold custody, refining and trading hub, followed by a response from Minister Chee Hong Tat on MAS's financial sector development work.
an-industrial-policy-in-finance.why_it_matters: The transcript states that Singapore's financial sector contributes around 14% of gross domestic product in 2025 and employs almost 200,000 people, more than 80% of whom are locals, with about 90% of net jobs created over the past decade going to locals. Mr Tiong's proposals on gold custody law, refining capacity and market standards were put forward as suggestions, and Mr Chee said he would take them on board. The record does not set out any decision taken on those proposals.

strengthening-support-and-dignity-for-mi.title: Adjournment debate on migrant domestic workers and caregiving support
strengthening-support-and-dignity-for-mi.what_it_is: An adjournment motion debate in which Ms Yeo Wan Ling set out proposals to support migrant domestic workers and caregiving families, and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Shawn Huang responded on behalf of the Government.
strengthening-support-and-dignity-for-mi.why_it_matters: For households with caregiving needs, the transcript records that the Home Caregiving Grant will increase to up to $600 per month and the per capita household income threshold will rise to $4,800 from April 2026. It also records that eligible households pay a $60 concessionary levy instead of $300, and that the minimum annual medical insurance claim limit for MDWs is $60,000. The record does not state whether the Member's other proposals will be implemented.

reforming-cca-access-in-our-schools.title: Adjournment debate on access to school co-curricular activities
reforming-cca-access-in-our-schools.what_it_is: An adjournment motion in which Mr Kenneth Tiong spoke on access to co-curricular activities and proposed reforms, followed by a response from Senior Minister of State for Education David Neo, before Parliament adjourned.
reforming-cca-access-in-our-schools.why_it_matters: The record sets out proposals to widen access to CCAs, including extending the primary school no-trial pilot to secondary schools, allowing students to change CCAs without LEAPS penalty, and expanding cross-school programmes. The Senior Minister of State said MOE and MCCY are working to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools, that students from lower-income families can tap the MOE Opportunity Fund for CCA expenses, and that strengthening access to CCAs is a key priority. He said more details will be announced at MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later.

structuring-singapore-for-flourishing-fa.title: Adjournment Motion on marriage and parenthood support
structuring-singapore-for-flourishing-fa.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion speech by Ms Elysa Chen on marriage and parenthood, followed by a response from Second Minister for National Development Ms Indranee Rajah.
structuring-singapore-for-flourishing-fa.why_it_matters: The record sets out proposals on leave, childcare, work, fertility and housing, and a Government update that the Marriage and Parenthood Reset Workgroup is developing a long-term roadmap. Ms Indranee Rajah said the Workgroup will study Ms Chen's suggestions and continue engagements. No immediate policy changes are stated in the transcript.

low-altitude-economy-building-the-flying.title: Adjournment Motion on developing a low-altitude economy and eVTOL industry in Singapore
low-altitude-economy-building-the-flying.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion debate in which Dr Neo Kok Beng set out opportunities and proposals for a low-altitude economy and eVTOL industry, and Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling responded on the Government’s approach.
low-altitude-economy-building-the-flying.why_it_matters: The transcript says drones are already used in Singapore for tasks such as ship-to-shore deliveries, tunnel and façade inspections, high-rise ledge cleaning and crowd monitoring, and that using drones for reservoir monitoring can potentially reduce required man-hours by up to 70%. It also says eVTOLs may not be viable extensively as a domestic transport option in Singapore, but could eventually be viable for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands or cross-border cargo transfer.

building-a-democracy-of-deeds.title: Adjournment motion with speeches on community participation and government partnerships
building-a-democracy-of-deeds.what_it_is: An adjournment motion moved by the Deputy Leader of the House, followed by speeches from Mr Foo Cexiang and Ms Goh Hanyan on community participation and government partnerships.
building-a-democracy-of-deeds.why_it_matters: For residents in the estates mentioned, the transcript describes local pilots: blue recycling bins removed in Seng Poh estate with collection drives, a participatory budgeting pilot in Spottiswoode Park with a $200,000 budget, and a digital art exhibition at the Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter. It also lists government funds and programmes intended to support citizen-led initiatives, such as the $50 million SG Partnerships Fund and expanded Heritage Activation Nodes. The record does not state any nationwide change in law or policy.

integration-with-the-region.title: Adjournment speech on deeper Singapore-Malaysia economic integration and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
integration-with-the-region.what_it_is: An adjournment motion debate in which MP Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat set out proposals for deeper economic integration with Malaysia and Southeast Asia, followed by a response from Minister of State for Trade and Industry Alvin Tan, before Parliament adjourned.
integration-with-the-region.why_it_matters: The transcript says the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link will arrive in 2027 carrying up to 10,000 passengers an hour each way, and cites a DBS estimate that $1.5 billion to $2.1 billion a year of retail spending could leak to Johor, with food and personal services hit hardest. It records that Singapore and Malaysia have jointly agreed to attract 50 projects in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone in five years and 100 in 10 years, and that Singapore and Singapore-based companies have committed over $5.5 billion in investments into Johor since a January 2024 Memorandum of Understanding.

singapore-energy-resilience-strategy-an-.title: Adjournment Motion on a national energy resilience strategy using solar and battery microgrids
singapore-energy-resilience-strategy-an-.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion moved by Mr Azhar Othman proposing a national energy resilience strategy based on decentralised off-grid and micro-grid power solutions with solar photovoltaic generation and battery energy storage, followed by a response from Minister of State Gan Siow Huang.
singapore-energy-resilience-strategy-an-.why_it_matters: Mr Azhar Othman said public housing estates, which house 80% of our population, largely lack any form of backup beyond emergency lighting in stairwells, and that when the grid fails lifts and water pumps stop. He proposed that solar plus battery storage keep essential loads such as lifts and water pumps running during outages. Ms Gan Siow Huang said microgrids are one of several distributed energy solutions that will be studied further, subject to safety requirements and technical standards.

protecting-resident-well-being-amidst-co.title: Adjournment Motion on protecting resident well-being amidst commercial activity
protecting-resident-well-being-amidst-co.what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion in which Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng raised resident disamenities from commercial activity in residential neighbourhoods and proposed six measures, followed by a response from Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling.
protecting-resident-well-being-amidst-co.why_it_matters: Residents in mixed-use neighbourhoods may be affected by noise, smell, safety and congestion from nearby commercial activity, and the debate sets out existing and proposed measures such as HDB tenancy conditions, quotas on licensed massage establishments, exclusion areas for new nightlife or massage outlets, and a review of massage establishment regulations. The transcript does not state a commencement date or final decision on the six proposals.

acknowledgement-to-the-chair.title: End-of-Budget speeches after Supply and Supplementary Bills pass
acknowledgement-to-the-chair.what_it_is: Speeches at the end of the formal Budget 2026 process, after the Supply Bill and Supplementary Bill were passed, with the Leader of the House acknowledging the Speaker and the Speaker reflecting on the debate.
acknowledgement-to-the-chair.stage: End of the formal Budget process for Budget 2026
acknowledgement-to-the-chair.why_it_matters: The record says Budget 2026 is intended to help Singaporeans navigate a changed world, with measures on AI adoption, economic strategy, workers, families, social compact, security and sustainability. It also says the projected $15.1 billion surplus for FY2025 provides ballast and buffer against potential turbulence, and that global developments may affect energy prices, business costs and daily costs of living.

strengthening-return-to-work-pathways.title: Adjournment motion on return-to-work support for injured and ill workers
strengthening-return-to-work-pathways.what_it_is: An adjournment motion in which Mr Melvin Yong spoke on strengthening return-to-work support for injured and ill workers, and the Minister of State for Manpower responded.
strengthening-return-to-work-pathways.why_it_matters: The transcript records proposals to strengthen return-to-work support and a planned MOM review, but it does not state any immediate change to entitlements or support for workers. MOM says it will launch an Alliance for Action on Safety and Health for Employment Longevity in the second half of 2026. The record does not set out the practical impact of these steps.

committee-of-supply-head-f-parliament.title: Proposed $100 cut to Head F of the Estimates withdrawn after debate on political integrity and grassroots advisers
committee-of-supply-head-f-parliament.what_it_is: A proposed $100 reduction to Head F of the Estimates, moved by Ms He Ting Ru and later withdrawn.
committee-of-supply-head-f-parliament.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact. The proposed $100 cut to Head F was withdrawn, and no change to funding or rules is stated.

report-of-the-commission-on-parliament-s.title: Parliament moves to revise terms of service for Parliament staff
report-of-the-commission-on-parliament-s.what_it_is: A motion moved by the Leader of the House asking Parliament to determine that the terms of service of Parliament staff under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) be revised in line with the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff.
report-of-the-commission-on-parliament-s.why_it_matters: The transcript states that Parliament staff on these two schemes will receive the same salary adjustments of 2% to 9% given to civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008), with effect from 1 August 2026. It also states that a retention payment component will be introduced for Parliamentary Clerks with effect from 1 September 2026. The stated aim is to keep the terms of service of Parliament staff competitive in attracting and retaining officers.

determination-on-committee-of-privileges.title: Ministerial statement on no further action over COP findings on Sylvia Lim and Faisal Manap
determination-on-committee-of-privileges.what_it_is: A Ministerial Statement by the Leader of the House on the Committee of Privileges findings about Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, concluding that no further action need be taken by the House because the PPIPA time-bar prevents penalties.
determination-on-committee-of-privileges.why_it_matters: The statement says the 15th Parliament cannot impose penalties under the PPIPA for this conduct because it took place in the First Session of the 14th Parliament. The Leader of the House says no further action need be taken by the House in relation to the Committee's finding regarding Ms Lim and Mr Faisal. The record does not set out the practical impact.

civil-list.title: Motion to adjust the Civil List for the President's office from FY2025
civil-list.what_it_is: A motion moved in Parliament under section 7 of the Civil List and Gratuity Act 1970 to vary the Schedule to that Act, raising three figures that fund the President's office.
civil-list.why_it_matters: The motion changes the amounts set aside for the President's personal staff, the household, and seconded public officers, with the changes taking effect from FY2025. The Minister stated that no change is proposed to the President's salary and allowance. The record does not set out the practical impact on ordinary people.

suspension-of-standing-orders-to-allow-s.title: Motion to lift speaking limits for the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill
suspension-of-standing-orders-to-allow-s.what_it_is: A procedural motion moved by the Leader of the House, and assented to by the Speaker and Members present, exempting two office-holders from the Standing Orders so they may speak more than once and without time limits during the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill.
suspension-of-standing-orders-to-allow-s.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

supplementary-estimates-of-expenditure-f.title: Supplementary Estimates of Expenditure for 2025-2026 taken en bloc in Committee of Supply
supplementary-estimates-of-expenditure-f.what_it_is: The reporting stage of Committee of Supply proceedings on the Supplementary Main Estimates and Supplementary Development Estimates for the financial year 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, followed by a motion that Parliament agree with the Committee's resolutions.
supplementary-estimates-of-expenditure-f.why_it_matters: The resolutions recorded in the transcript supply $1,087,355,800 to the Government under the Heads of Expenditure in the Supplementary Main Estimates and $2,161,019,900 under the Head of Expenditure in the Supplementary Development Estimates, for public services in the financial year 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. The transcript does not say which services the money goes to or what changes for individuals.

committee-of-supply-total-sums-for-main-.title: Committee of Supply resolutions on FY2026/27 Main and Development Estimates
committee-of-supply-total-sums-for-main-.what_it_is: A report of Committee of Supply resolutions and a motion for Parliament to agree to supply $158,962,520,000 under the Main Estimates and $49,014,559,600 under the Development Estimates for the financial year 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
committee-of-supply-total-sums-for-main-.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

estimates-of-expenditure-of-singapore-fo.title: Procedural opening of Committee of Supply debate on FY2026 Estimates
estimates-of-expenditure-of-singapore-fo.what_it_is: This is the procedural opening of the Committee of Supply debate on the FY2026 Main and Development Estimates; the transcript contains no policy substance.
estimates-of-expenditure-of-singapore-fo.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

supply-bill.title: Supply Bill gives legislative approval for government spending from April 2026 to March 2027
supply-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, and then Third Reading, that gives legislative approval for appropriations from the Consolidated Fund and the Development Fund to meet expenditure for the financial year 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
supply-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill gives legislative approval for appropriations from the Consolidated Fund and Development Fund for the year 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Once approved, it empowers the Minister to issue warrants authorising expenditure up to the amount for each Head as shown in the Bill to be paid out from those funds.

grant-to-imf-s-trust-for-special-poverty.title: Parliament approves maximum grant for Sudan debt relief via IMF trust
grant-to-imf-s-trust-for-special-poverty.what_it_is: A motion under section 6A(2)(d) of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act 1966, moved by Minister of State for Trade and Industry Alvin Tan on behalf of the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister-in-charge of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, setting the maximum amount MAS may give under a bilateral agreement with the International Monetary Fund to support Sudan's debt relief efforts.
grant-to-imf-s-trust-for-special-poverty.why_it_matters: The resolution caps the grant that the Monetary Authority of Singapore may give under a bilateral agreement with the International Monetary Fund at 4,480,000 Special Drawing Rights (approximately US$6,100,000). The money is to support Sudan's debt relief efforts via the Trust for Special Poverty Reduction and Growth Operations for the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries. The record does not set out further practical impact for people in Singapore.

rearrangement-of-business.title: Business Motion to take AI transition motion after SWDA Bill
rearrangement-of-business.what_it_is: A Business Motion moved by the Deputy Leader of the House to rearrange the order of business so that a Private Member's Motion on an AI transition with no jobless growth is taken immediately after proceedings on the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) Bill.
rearrangement-of-business.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

supplementary-supply-fy2025-bill.title: Bill for additional expenditure beyond the Supply Act 2025
supplementary-supply-fy2025-bill.what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading and Third Reading that makes additional provision for expenditure in excess of sums authorised by the Supply Act 2025, using additional sums approved in the Supplementary Estimates of Expenditure for the financial year 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
supplementary-supply-fy2025-bill.why_it_matters: The Bill authorises additional government expenditure beyond the sums in the Supply Act 2025 for the financial year 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. The transcript does not set out the practical impact for ordinary people.

committee-of-supply-heads-b-c-d-e-g-and-.title: Approval of remaining expenditure heads in the Main and Development Estimates
committee-of-supply-heads-b-c-d-e-g-and-.what_it_is: A procedural stage in the Committee of Supply's consideration of the 2026 Estimates, in which the remaining Heads of Expenditure with no amendments on the Order Paper Supplement were put to the Committee en bloc and agreed to without debate.
committee-of-supply-heads-b-c-d-e-g-and-.why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.
